all_facts: > Three nodes are 2.6× slower than one.
The DMA ring does 4462 MiB/s CPU-free.
The problem is serialization, not bandwidth.
llama.cpp has no tensor-parallel RPC backend.
Three independent workers scale 2.96x.
The card out-serves the host outright.
Pipelined node-to-node throughput is up to 4423 MiB/s
Same pair, same day, same jumbo MTU
DMA pipelined ring throughput is 2020 MiB/s (16.9 Gbit/s) from node 1 to node 2
DMA pipelined ring throughput is 4423 MiB/s (37.1 Gbit/s) from node 2 to node 1
Against old MTU-1500 baseline, ring is 6.1x–13.8x
Against jumbo virtio, ring is roughly 1.4x–2.2x on throughput
It is consistent
First working version managed only 2025 MiB/s
Sender refilled 512 KiB of local buffer with CPU memset-style loop every iteration
DMA payload fill was the bottleneck, not the fabric
dma_sync_wait() the payload before writing the flag
Flag is a CPU write through the BAR while payload goes via DMA engine
Counters are monotonic
Ready-flag handshake and fields kept clear of offset 0
Order handshake: clear ready, zero counters, publish ready last
The rtnl self-deadlock caused host wedges where SSH never completed logins.
The deadlock occurred because register_netdevice() invoked the netdev notifier chain with rtnl already held.
rtnl_lock() is not recursive, causing a NETDEV_REGISTER handler to self-deadlock.
The deadlock happened inside the VOP workqueue and left rtnl held forever.
The handler fired when a NIC registered while the module was loaded, i.e. during a node reboot.
Benchmarking never reboots a node, so it never tripped the issue.
apply_dev() was fixed to take an explicit rtnl_held flag and use netif_set_mtu() instead of dev_set_mtu().
Verification by rebooting a node with the module loaded showed release and re-apply both logged with zero blocked lines and zero D-state.
The host journal is persistent and journalctl -b -1 -k shows the previous boot's kernel log including the stack trace that preceded the wedge.
Three power cycles were spent guessing at causes before anyone looked.
Mutating `req->bio->bi_iter.bi_sector` was a real latent bug
